topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Which classical dance form originated in Tamil Nadu and is traditionally associated with temple dancers (devadasis)?
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest classical dance forms, originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu and was historically performed by devadasis. It is characterised by fixed upper-body posture, bent knees (aramandi), intricate footwork, and expressive hand gestures (mudras). It was revived in the 20th century by Rukmini Devi Arundale.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Kathakali, known for its elaborate make-up and costumes, is the classical dance-drama of which state?
questions.explanation: Kathakali is the classical dance-drama of Kerala, famous for its elaborate facial make-up (with colour codes — green 'pacha' for noble characters), towering costumes, and stories from the epics. The make-up colour denotes character type. Kerala's other classical form is Mohiniyattam (the 'dance of the enchantress').
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Which classical dance form is associated with North India and was patronised in the courts of Mughal and Rajput rulers, known for its spins (chakkars) and footwork?
questions.explanation: Kathak, the classical dance of North India (UP, Rajasthan), evolved from storytelling traditions (the word derives from 'katha', meaning story) and flourished in Mughal and Rajput courts. It is known for rapid pirouettes (chakkars), rhythmic footwork with ankle bells (ghungroos), and gharanas like Lucknow, Jaipur and Banaras.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Bhangra is a vigorous folk dance associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Bhangra is the energetic harvest folk dance of Punjab, traditionally performed during Baisakhi. It is accompanied by the dhol drum. Its female counterpart is Giddha. Bhangra has become globally popular and is a staple of celebrations across the Punjabi diaspora.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: The classical dance form 'Odissi' originated in which state?
questions.explanation: Odissi originated in Odisha and is one of the oldest surviving classical dance forms, depicted in the sculptures of the Konark Sun Temple and Jagannath Temple at Puri. It is characterised by the tribhanga (three-bend) posture and chowk stance, with fluid, sculpturesque movements often depicting themes from the Gita Govinda.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Garba and Dandiya Raas are folk dances associated with which state, performed especially during Navratri?
questions.explanation: Garba and Dandiya Raas are the iconic folk dances of Gujarat, performed during the nine nights of Navratri. Garba involves circular movements around a lamp or image of the goddess; Dandiya Raas uses decorated sticks. In 2023, Garba was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Which classical dance form originated in Andhra Pradesh and takes its name from the village where it developed?
questions.explanation: Kuchipudi originated in the village of Kuchipudi (Kuchelapuram) in Andhra Pradesh, from which it takes its name. It blends dance, drama, and song, and was traditionally performed by male Brahmin troupes (Bhagavatas). A distinctive feature is the 'tarangam', where the dancer performs on the edges of a brass plate.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Sattriya, recognised as a classical dance form in 2000, is associated with which state and was created by which saint?

options.text: West Bengal; created by Chaitanya Mahaprabhu

questions.explanation: Sattriya originated in Assam and was created in the 15th century by the Vaishnavite saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardev as part of devotional practice in the 'sattras' (monasteries). It was recognised as a classical dance form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, the most recent addition to the classical canon.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Mohiniyattam, a graceful solo dance performed by women, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Mohiniyattam ('dance of the enchantress', from Mohini, the female avatar of Vishnu) is a classical dance of Kerala, performed traditionally as a solo by women. It features gentle, swaying movements (like swaying palm trees) and is distinct from Kerala's other classical form, the vigorous Kathakali.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: The 'Manipuri' classical dance is best known for which themed performance?
questions.explanation: Manipuri classical dance, from Manipur, is renowned for its Raas Leela performances depicting the divine love of Radha and Krishna. It is characterised by gentle, graceful, flowing movements, with the female dancer wearing a distinctive stiff barrel-shaped skirt (kumil). It avoids the sharp foot-stamping of other classical forms.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: 'Bihu' is the folk dance associated with which festival and state?
questions.explanation: Bihu is the folk dance of Assam, performed during the Bihu festival (especially Rongali/Bohag Bihu, the Assamese New Year and spring harvest festival in April). It is a lively group dance with brisk steps and rapid hand movements, accompanied by the dhol, pepa (hornpipe), and gogona.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: The folk dances 'Ghoomar' and 'Kalbeliya' belong to which state?
questions.explanation: Both Ghoomar and Kalbeliya are folk dances of Rajasthan. Ghoomar is a graceful twirling dance performed by women in flowing ghagras. Kalbeliya, performed by the Kalbeliya (snake-charmer) community, was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010 and features serpentine body movements.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Which dance form is a martial-art-based performance from Kerala / nearby regions, sometimes classed as a semi-classical/folk form?
questions.explanation: Theyyam is a ritualistic dance-worship form of northern Kerala, where the performer is believed to embody a deity, wearing elaborate face paint and towering headgear. Chhau (Jharkhand/Odisha/Bengal) is a martial dance and a UNESCO heritage form. Yakshagana is a Karnataka dance-drama; Lavani is a Maharashtrian folk dance.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: 'Lavani', a folk dance known for powerful rhythm and traditionally performed to the beats of the dholki, is associated with which state?
questions.explanation: Lavani is a popular folk dance and music form of Maharashtra, traditionally performed by women in nine-yard saris to the beat of the dholki drum. It is known for its powerful rhythm and has been a prominent feature of Marathi theatre (Tamasha). Its themes range from the romantic to the socio-political.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: The 'Chhau' dance, recognised by UNESCO, is a tradition shared by which group of states?
questions.explanation: Chhau is a semi-classical martial dance with three regional styles: Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha), and Purulia Chhau (West Bengal). The Seraikella and Purulia styles use masks. It was inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010 and often depicts episodes from the epics.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: How many dance forms are officially recognised as 'classical' by the Sangeet Natak Akademi (commonly cited count)?
questions.explanation: Eight dance forms are commonly recognised as classical: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur), Mohiniyattam (Kerala), and Sattriya (Assam). (Some sources also count Chhau, but the standard exam answer is eight.)
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: 'Yakshagana', a traditional theatre form combining dance, music, and dialogue, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Yakshagana is a traditional dance-drama theatre form of coastal Karnataka, combining dance, music, song, elaborate costumes, and improvised dialogue, usually performed overnight depicting episodes from the epics and Puranas. It is distinct from the classical eight but is a celebrated folk-theatre tradition.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: The folk dances 'Cheraw' (bamboo dance) is associated with which northeastern state?
questions.explanation: Cheraw, the famous bamboo dance, is the traditional folk dance of Mizoram. Dancers step rhythmically between bamboo staves that are clapped together by people sitting on the ground. It is one of the oldest Mizo dances, performed on festive occasions, and requires precise timing to avoid the moving bamboo.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Which dance is the folk dance of Jammu & Kashmir, performed by women in groups?
questions.explanation: Rouf (Rauf) is a traditional folk dance of Jammu & Kashmir, performed by women in two facing rows during spring and festivals like Eid. Nati is a folk dance of Himachal Pradesh; Dollu Kunitha is a drum dance of Karnataka; Jhumar is associated with Punjab/Haryana and tribal regions.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Which of the following is the folk dance of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Nati is the famous folk dance of Himachal Pradesh, particularly the Kullu region. A form of Nati once entered the Guinness World Records as the largest folk dance. It is performed during festivals and fairs, with slow rhythmic movements in a circle. Bihu is Assamese, Garba is Gujarati, and the bamboo dance (Cheraw) is from Mizoram.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: A question matches classical dances to states. Which pairing is INCORRECT?
questions.explanation: Option C is INCORRECT. Mohiniyattam belongs to KERALA, not Karnataka. The other pairings are correct: Kuchipudi → Andhra Pradesh, Sattriya → Assam, Odissi → Odisha. Note that Kerala has TWO classical forms (Kathakali and Mohiniyattam), which is a frequent exam point.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Which classical dance form's repertoire follows the sequence Alarippu → Jatiswaram → Shabdam → Varnam → Padam → Tillana?
questions.explanation: This is the traditional 'Margam' repertoire sequence of Bharatanatyam: Alarippu (invocation), Jatiswaram (pure dance), Shabdam, Varnam (the centrepiece combining nritta and abhinaya), Padam (expressive), and Tillana (rhythmic finale). Knowing this margam structure distinguishes Bharatanatyam from the other classical forms.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: The 'gharanas' of Lucknow, Jaipur, and Banaras are associated with which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Kathak has three major gharanas (stylistic schools): Lucknow (emphasis on grace and abhinaya/expression), Jaipur (emphasis on vigorous footwork and rhythm), and Banaras (Janaki Prasad gharana). The Raigarh gharana is sometimes added. The gharana system reflects Kathak's evolution through court patronage.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Rukmini Devi Arundale is credited with reviving and de-stigmatising which classical dance form, also founding the Kalakshetra institution?
questions.explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale revived Bharatanatyam in the early 20th century, bringing it from the devadasi temple tradition to a respectable concert stage, and founded the Kalakshetra Foundation in Chennai (1936). She is also remembered for declining the offer to become President of India. Her work was pivotal in the dance's national revival.
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India

questions.stem: Which treatise, attributed to Bharata Muni, is considered the foundational text for Indian classical dance and dramaturgy?
questions.explanation: The Natya Shastra, attributed to Bharata Muni (compiled roughly between 200 BCE and 200 CE), is the foundational Sanskrit treatise on the performing arts — dance, drama, and music — and defines concepts like rasa (aesthetic emotion) and bhava. The Abhinaya Darpana (by Nandikeshvara) is a later, more specialised text on gestures (mudras).
questions.subject: General Knowledge
questions.topic: Classical and Folk Dances of India
